title: Hole cycles: fine boring (oriented stop, shift off the wall, rapid out) with user-given orientation and shift

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Part of #1445.

The first slice of #1445 (the ream, G85) left fine boring out on purpose. A fine-boring cycle stops the spindle at a fixed orientation at the bottom, shifts the tip away from the wall, then rapids out. The shift direction and amount depend on how the boring bar is clamped relative to the spindle's orientation angle. A guessed default could drag the tip across the finished bore, so no default is posted.

What is owed:
- A drill-op cycle choice for fine boring, with two required user parameters: the shift direction (or angle) and the shift amount, validated at command creation (finite, positive amount, smaller than the hole radius minus the tool's tip extent).
- A machine capability for oriented spindle stop; a machine or post without it refuses the cycle by name, never posts a plain bore in its place.
- Posts that have the canned word write it, with the shift words in that control's own form; the others refuse by name (an expanded chain needs M19-style orientation, which is per control).
- The CL chain the verifier and simulation read: feed in, (dwell), shift, rapid out, so the rapid out is judged against the wall at the shifted position.
- MCP `edit_operation` parameters for both values, a UI row in plain English.

Sources: public controller documentation only (RS-274/NGC, LinuxCNC; vendor programming manuals for the word layout). RS-274/NGC uses G76 for lathe threading; the fine-boring word differs by control and must be read from each post, not assumed.

Done means: fine boring is a user choice that posts only with an orientation-capable machine and an explicit shift, is refused by name otherwise, and is pinned by per-post goldens and a verifier test of the shifted retract.
